The problem

You have fixed six things this year. The pressure has not moved.

That is not a discipline problem. It is a diagnosis problem.

Your business is not broken. It may simply have outgrown the way it was built. Every part of it still functions. None of it fits any more, because the operating model hasn’t caught up with the growth.

Here is how owners say it out loud.

  • "If my business is growing, then why am I making less money?"
  • "I don’t own my business. My business owns me."
  • "Everyone gets to take a vacation but me."
  • "All I do is put out other people’s fires all day long."
  • "I am the only one who knows how everything works."

Symptoms are loud. Causes are quiet. So owners treat the loudest thing in the room, feel briefly better, and watch the same pressure resurface somewhere else three months later.

Before deciding what to change, understand what is actually happening in the business.
Why work with Veronica

When you hire a specialist, the solution is often already decided. The diagnosis tends to follow.

Get’em There sits upstream of that decision. The diagnosis is not built to justify a solution chosen in advance.

A marketing agency looks through a marketing lens. A recruiter looks through a hiring lens. An AI consultant looks through an automation lens. That is what you hired them to do. The problem is hiring one before you know what actually needs fixing.

Veronica starts before that decision, with no answer already in mind. She reads across the financials, the operations, the people, the pricing, the systems, the capacity and the marketing, and lets the evidence choose the recommendation.

Sometimes the recommendation is to spend nothing and change one decision. When the work calls for more, she can implement, oversee execution, or stay on in an advisory role.

She has run the thing she is advising you on.

As Manager of Business Operations, she was the Swiss Army Knife of a growing company, wearing whichever hat the business needed that day.

She reads a business at any size.

Enterprise grade analysis from inside a top ten United States bank, grounded in years of running small and fast-growing companies.

She looks across the whole business, not one department.

Finance, operations, people, technology, marketing and capacity, and how each affects the others. What comes back is what matters most, not twenty things that could be improved.

She cannot leave an unanswered question alone.

Her sixth grade class gave her an award for asking why, and a former boss nicknamed her The Digger. Twenty-five years later, nothing has changed.

She is easy to be honest with.

Nothing about her makes you feel behind for not having solved this already.

The answer isn’t always another person, another system, or another tool. Start by understanding the problem you’re actually trying to solve.

How the work gets done

Five questions that keep the investigation grounded.

The Foundation Framework. Gather. Evaluate. Target.

This is not a checklist worked in order. Veronica follows whatever does not sound right, wherever it leads. These questions keep her oriented along the way, so the business does not end up buying the wrong solution beautifully.

  • 1. Set the destination

    What do you actually want this business to become? Every option is measured against your answer, not against somebody else’s definition of growth.

  • 2. Get your bearings

    What is objectively true about the business today? Not what you assume. Not what you hope. What the numbers, the workflows and the people actually show.

  • 3. Read the signals

    What stands out, what does not fit, what evidence is missing, and what is being assumed? This is where symptoms get separated from causes.

  • 4. Find what matters most

    What is most likely limiting the business right now, or about to? Sometimes it is one issue. Often it is several, connected. That is where the leverage sits.

  • 5. Chart the course

    What should you do next, what are the tradeoffs, and why? A short ordered list you can start on Monday.

  • There can be more than one way forward. The goal is to understand the tradeoffs and determine which route makes the most sense for your business.

What owners say

Owners rarely describe the strategy. They describe the relief.

The belief behind the work

A bigger business is not automatically a better one.

Growth is supposed to buy you profit, capacity and time. If it is buying complexity, something upstream is wrong.

What carried your business to this size was built for a smaller business. That is not a failure. That is what growth does to a company that is working.

There is no single formula, which is why Get’em There does not sell one. The right route depends on your business, on you, and on where you actually want to end up. We find yours and we say so plainly, including when the honest answer is that you are closer than you think.

You don’t need to fix everything. You need to know where attention can create the greatest impact.
About Veronica

She has already been the person holding a scaling company together.

Veronica Redmond. Strategic Business Advisor.

Her start was hands on. She built the processes and ran operations in one of her family’s businesses, after working as a retail store manager, in inside and outside sales, and as a warehouse inventory control foreman.

Veronica was then employee number one at a company that grew from roughly $500,000 to $5 million, serving as its financial and operational leader. Her job was whatever the owners could not carry.

  • Operations.
  • Accounting.
  • Forecasting and cost analysis.
  • HR and payroll.
  • Systems and process.
  • Software design and development.
  • Technology selection and implementation.
  • Data migration.
  • Market analysis for expansion.
  • Marketing project management.

Since then she has seen businesses at every stage, from startups and small businesses to fast-scaling companies and enterprise environments. She has seen what changes as organizations grow, and what can stop working when they do.

She launched Get’em There in 2009 and spent nearly eight years working directly with small business owners on growth, operations, workflows, SOPs, hiring and systems. She closed it when her children reached college and she needed predictable income. In the years that followed she moved through controller roles, including leading finance and HR at a second multi-location company. She then went into enterprise strategy, working across finance, technology, automation, product and large scale transformation.

Get’em There is back, built differently this time.

Veronica brings big-company rigor to businesses that would never be able to hire an enterprise consultant, and she brings small business realism to work that usually arrives as theory.

She is also the founder of GET Acquainted, a community that brings entrepreneurs together to build relationships and visibility, and the host of GET Acquainted Live.

What worked to get your business here may not be what it needs to get where you want to go next.
